subject: Operational handback acknowledgement & evidence packet request
messages:
From: Daniel Rivera <daniel.rivera@fortitech.io>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: eng+ops@fortitech.io
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment SLA — operational handback and evidence packet request

Jonas,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. As discussed, FortiTech needs explicit language in the Private/VPC SLA that acknowledges the operational handback for our customer-controlled edge (WAN routers and transit peering). We are happy to accept that Redwood remains responsible for the inference runtime inside the VPC, but we need: 1) a short appendix that limits Redwood's latency/uptime obligations for traffic transiting our edge routers and 2) the evidence packet your team needs to validate that the root cause for incidents is on our side.

Requested evidence list (initial):
- BGP session flaps (RIB/adj-RIB-out snapshots) around incident windows
- Traceroutes from our egress IPs to Redwood ingestion endpoints
- sFlow/NetFlow samples (5-min window) for candidate incidents
- TLS handshake logs (timestamps + cert IDs) when relevant

Can you confirm Redwood's acceptable evidence format, any retention/certification requirements, and a proposed short clause we can include in our contracting appendix? We are trying to close procurement by quarter end and need this to feed legal.

Attaching a sanitized trace bundle from 2028-02-28 for your engineering review.

Best,
Daniel Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering
FortiTech

[Attachment: customer_network_trace_20280228.zip]

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Rivera <daniel.rivera@fortitech.io>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA — operational handback and evidence packet request

Daniel —

Appreciate the clear list and the trace bundle. We can accommodate an "operational handback" appendix that: (a) documents which network/edge components are customer-controlled, (b) clarifies that latency and availability attributable to those components are outside Redwood's uptime SLA measurement window, and (c) defines the minimal evidence set required to attribute incidents to customer-controlled infrastructure.

Quick notes / asks from our side:
- Format: we prefer compressed PCAP + a short JSON manifest (timestamp ranges, observed IPs, ports) for trace evidence. The Zip you sent looked good but please keep any PII or internal hostnames sanitized.
- Time sync: all evidence should include NTP/chrony offsets to +/- 1s if possible; it helps match our ingestion logs for KV cache warmup sequences.
- Measurement windows: for latency attribution we use 1-minute and 5-minute rolling percentiles; please include raw traceroutes sampled at both peak and normal traffic times.
- Legal: Kimberly, can you draft a single-paragraph appendix we can circulate to FortiTech Legal?

I'll loop in Engineering to validate the trace bundle and propose accepted file formats. If engineering signs off, legal can mirror the language and we can finalize the contract appendix. Tone: keep it short and operational — nothing that shifts Redwood's runtime obligations.

Jonas
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

[Attachment referenced: proposed_handback_clause_v1.docx (to be attached once Kimberly provides the draft)]

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Daniel Rivera <daniel.rivera@fortitech.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA — operational handback and evidence packet request

Daniel / team —

Draft language below (one paragraph). Happy to iterate, but this keeps the appendix short and defensible for both sides: 

"Operational handback: Customer-operated network elements (including but not limited to WAN routers, transit peering, and customer-managed edge proxies) are excluded from Redwood Inference's uptime and tail-latency commitments for any portion of request/response latency that is demonstrably attributable to those elements. Determination of attribution shall be based on mutually agreed evidence (traceroutes, BGP session logs, packet captures, and TLS handshake timestamps). Where attribution is established to customer-controlled infrastructure, Redwood's obligation will be limited to diagnostic support and recommended mitigations; no SLA credit shall be due for the portion of latency or unavailability attributable to customer-controlled components."

Operational notes for evidence: please provide packet captures in zipped PCAP format, BGP RIB snapshots covering the incident window, and at least two traceroutes from different egress POPs. Please also include the edge-router config snippet that shows any policy-based routing that might affect traffic to our endpoints.

If that sounds reasonable, Daniel, please confirm and we'll attach a clean DOCX for your counsel. 

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: proposed_handback_clause_v1.docx]

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Daniel Rivera <daniel.rivera@fortitech.io>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA — operational handback and evidence packet request

Daniel / team —

Engineering reviewed the trace bundle. Summary: the 2028-02-28 capture shows clear asymmetric routing at the customer edge (ASN 63721) and intermittent BGP adj-flaps that line up with the latency spikes to our ingestion POP in us-west-2. We can accept the evidence as prima facie for attribution pending the following: (1) sanitized PCAPs with full 5-minute pre/post windows for two incidents, (2) RIB snapshots with timestamps and origin-AS verification, and (3) confirmation of NTP sync on the edge routers.

We also attached an example of the minimal config snippet we need (see edge_router_config_snippet.txt) — primarily to confirm whether policy-based routing or per-prefix shunting is in play. If FortiTech can deliver those three items, engineering will produce a short technical finding statement we can include in the appendix as a signed exhibit.

Marissa Cole
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: edge_router_config_snippet.txt]

From: Daniel Rivera <daniel.rivera@fortitech.io>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment SLA — operational handback and evidence packet request

Thanks everyone — this is helpful and aligns with what we expected. We'll produce the sanitized PCAPs, RIB snapshots, and an NTP verification report by COB next Wednesday (2028-03-08). Our legal is okay with the one-paragraph appendix as written; I approved the language internally and they asked for the engineering finding exhibit before signing.

I'll upload the artifacts to the shared Drive folder and send the link here when ready. Appreciate the quick turnaround — this will unblock procurement.

—Daniel
Head of Platform Engineering, FortiTech

[Attachments to follow: customer_network_trace_20280228.zip (already sent); new artifacts to be uploaded to shared Drive]
